title: Topic 10 · Living Authentically · Chunks
source: Modern Wisdom · Chris Williamson & Naval Ravikant · youtu.be/KyfUysrNaco

items.s: I asked him why, and he said, “I started feeling like I had to live up to in private the things that I was saying in public.”

items.c: the things that I was saying in public
items.s: I asked him why, and he said, “I started feeling like I had to live up to in private the things that I was saying in public.”

Mostly it’s about the AI AGI thing, and I think I’m still right about that, but it’s a different story.
It’s funny how people latch onto single proclamations, but the reality is all of us are dynamical systems.
I think people can smell that.

items.c: they want to be seen as something
items.s: What this world really lacks right now is authenticity and because everybody wants something They want to be seen as something, they want to be something that they're not.
If someone is wrong, no big deal, as long as they have a genuine reason for saying what they’re saying or believing what they’re believing.
And that’s a mistake not just for the listener, it's a mistake for themselves, because then you’re going to get trapped in a hall of mirrors.
For example, I did this Joe Rogan podcast, I don’t know, eight or nine years ago, and people will call out like the one thing that didn’t turn out to be correct.

items.c: works through making guesses and correcting errors
items.zh: 通过不断猜测、纠错来运作
items.note: work through + -ing 在此表示通过某种过程推进；注意与 work through a problem 的常见用法区别。
items.s: Every knowledge creation system works through making guesses and correcting errors.

items.note: A or B + 时间 + ago，自然口语里表示约数。
items.s: For example, I did this Joe Rogan podcast, I don’t know, eight or nine years ago, and people will call out like the one thing that didn’t turn out to be correct.

items.c: call out like the one thing
items.zh: 就揪出那么一件事来说
items.note: call out 已有词卡；这里 like 是口语填充/近似表达，别误译为“喜欢”。
items.s: For example, I did this Joe Rogan podcast, I don’t know, eight or nine years ago, and people will call out like the one thing that didn’t turn out to be correct.

items.c: I caught him in an error
items.note: catch someone in + 名词，注意原文这里说的是 error，不必自动理解成撒谎。
items.s: They just beat on it because it helps them in their mind raise their status a little bit – “I caught him in an error.”

items.note: make a guess at + something，从名词 guess 学到可用的搭配。
items.s: But on the other hand, if they just made a guess at something and they got it wrong.

items.note: get + it + adjective 表示判断结果；与 get it right 成对记。
items.s: But on the other hand, if they just made a guess at something and they got it wrong.

items.c: what you don’t want to be doing is
items.note: what ... is ... 聚焦重点；这里的进行形式强调行为，不是过去时。
items.s: But what you don’t want to be doing is lying in public because you’re trying to look good.

items.c: What this world really lacks right now is
items.zh: 这个世界现在真正缺少的是……
items.note: What ... is ... 强调结构；可以迁移到口语表达观点。
items.s: What this world really lacks right now is authenticity, because everybody wants something.

items.zh: 一个与真实自己不符的样子
items.note: something + that 关系从句；不是“不是什么东西”。
items.s: They want to be seen as something, they want to be something that they’re not.

items.c: saying things that they don’t really believe
items.zh: 说一些自己其实并不相信的话
items.note: things that ... 限定说的是哪种话；与言行一致主题紧密相关。
items.s: So you catch a lot of people saying things that they don’t really believe, and I think people are very sensitive to that.

items.c: whether or not this person means the thing that they’re saying
items.zh: 这个人说的话究竟是不是真心的
items.note: whether or not 是间接疑问；mean 是“真心表达”，不是“意思是”。
items.s: Bullshit radars have become hypersensitized to try and work out whether or not this person means the thing that they’re saying.

items.c: There’s a difference between being wrong and disingenuous though
items.zh: 不过，判断错和不真诚是两回事
items.note: difference between A and B，两边都是 being + adjective，注意 though 句末转折。
items.s: There’s a difference between being wrong and disingenuous though.

items.c: to live up to some expectation
items.note: live up to + expectation 是高频搭配；与 R01 自己说过的话所形成的标准对比。
items.s: But if they are lying to elevate their status or their appearance or to live up to some expectation, that’s the mistake.

items.c: get trapped in a hall of mirrors
items.zh: 陷入真假难辨的镜子迷宫
items.note: get trapped in + situation 可迁移到 get trapped in a cycle；这里是比喻。
items.s: And that’s a mistake not just for the listener, it's a mistake for themselves, because then you’re going to get trapped in a hall of mirrors.

items.note: 结合后面的 it's a mistake for themselves 理解“对听众和说话者自己都有害”。
items.s: And that’s a mistake not just for the listener, it's a mistake for themselves, because then you’re going to get trapped in a hall of mirrors.

items.c: be consistent with your past proclamations
items.zh: 与过去公开说过的话保持一致
items.note: be consistent with + something，可用于观点、行为、数据等；比单记 consistent 更实用。
items.s: You yourself are going to be consistent with your past proclamations, so if you’re lying to others, you’re going to be lying to yourself.

items.c: trying to impress people who don’t care about you
items.zh: 努力让那些根本不在乎你的人对你刮目相看
items.note: impress someone 不是“讨好”的固定同义词；强调给别人留下好印象。
items.s: You’re basically trying to impress people who don’t care about you.

items.c: don’t get to see the real you
items.zh: 没有机会看到真实的你
items.note: get to + verb 表示“有机会/能够”，不是 get 的“拿到”。
items.s: And the people who would like the real you don’t get to see the real you, so they pass you by.

items.zh: 他们就这样与你擦肩而过
items.note: pass someone by 也可表示机会悄悄错过。
items.s: And the people who would like the real you don’t get to see the real you, so they pass you by.

items.c: the very, very few people that you respect
items.zh: 那极少数真正受到你尊重的人
items.note: the very few 强调数量少，that you respect 修饰 people；别把 very 当作“非常尊重”。
items.s: You only want the respect of the very, very few people that you respect.

items.note: demand something from someone，与 earn someone's respect 对照（后者是拓展，不是采访原文）。
items.s: Trying to demand respect from the masses is a fool’s errand.

items.zh: 有意思的是…… / 真有意思，居然……
items.note: It's + adjective + how + 从句，表达对现象的观察和评价。
items.s: It’s funny how people latch onto single proclamations, but the reality is all of us are dynamical systems.
